questions.question_text: Relational exchange includes principle of reputation and repetition.
questions.explanation: Relational Exchange includes principles of Reputation and Repetition. Relational exchange relies on repeated interactions (future income outweighs cheating) and reputation (social consequences in networks).

questions.question_text: "Guild Secrets" are censored information of merchant guilds.
questions.explanation: Guild Secrets are censored information of merchant guilds. Guilds acted as cliques that restricted information flow to outsiders to maintain their monopoly/advantage. However, originally guild secrets were rich conduits of information, but later guilds became exclusive and censored information.

questions.question_text: While contract-based exchange is supposed to be impersonal or generalized, relational and power-based exchange is particularized and built around a person's identity.
Evolution of business is closely linked to how forms of exchange evolve.
questions.explanation: The evolution of business is closely linked to how forms of Exchange evolve. The shift from relational/power exchange to contractual exchange defines the history of business evolution.

questions.question_text: Contractual exchange increases investments in general.
The joint-stock companies were precursors to modern public multinational corporations.
questions.explanation: The joint-stock companies were precursors to modern public multinational corporations. Joint Stock Companies combined formalization of the firm and emergence of the stock market, allowing pooling investment from thousands of strangers and creating separation between Owners and Managers, which is the foundation of modern corporations.

questions.question_text: Relational and power-based exchange have dominated traditional business.
Joint stock companies combined the two innovations of generalized institutions: formalization of the firm, and the emergence of the stock market.
questions.explanation: Joint stock companies combined the two innovations of generalized institutions: formalization of the firm (defined ownership of assets) and the emergence of the stock market (ability to buy/sell shares). This allowed pooling investment from thousands of strangers and created separation between Owners (Shareholders) and Managers (CEOs/Board).

questions.question_text: After 1500s and especially after 1750s, uncharacteristic hockey stick of exponential growth happened.
As a clan is larger, more diverse set of skills can be taught to a child.
questions.explanation: As a clan is larger, a more diverse set of skills can be taught to a child. A larger network (Clan/Guild) offers more variety in expertise compared to a single family unit. Clan- or guild-based teaching exposes the child to wider expertise than the family alone.

questions.question_text: Hobbes believed that Human nature was selfish, and given this nature, a "common power" like a state was needed to make two strangers A and B, who are not members of the same community or firm, uphold their promises to each other.
Financial development has not had a unidirectional flow of progress throughout history.
questions.explanation: Financial development has not had a unidirectional flow of progress throughout history. Progress isn't natural - market development requires deliberate effort and can regress if the three core ingredients (Openness, Contractual Infrastructure, and Civic Norms) are not maintained.

questions.question_text: The job of a firm is to minimize competition, increase entry barriers and maximize profit.
Pro-Market policies are meant to be impartial towards all business and are supposed to increase competition by making it easy to do business or get a job.
questions.explanation: Pro-Market policies are meant to be impartial towards all business and are supposed to increase competition by making it easy to do business or get a job. Pro-Market policies favor competition, transparency, and low entry barriers for all, unlike Pro-Business policies which favor specific firms/incumbents.

questions.question_text: A common law heritage like England and its colonies had better protection for investors especially small investors that led to better capital markets.
questions.explanation: A common law heritage like England and its colonies had better protection for investors especially small investors that led to better capital markets. Common Law (e.g., UK, USA, India) provides better protection for small investors, leading to deeper capital markets compared to Civil Law systems.

questions.question_text: In regions with civil law heritage where law was codified by politicians, and where courts didn't enjoy any power to set precedent, the laws were more prone to capture by special interest, and more hostile to investor protection.
questions.explanation: In regions with civil law heritage where law was codified by politicians, and where courts didn't enjoy any power to set precedent, the laws were more prone to capture by special interest, and more hostile to investor protection. Civil Law is more codified/bureaucratic and often prone to capture by special interests, unlike Common Law which provides better investor protection.
